viewport_comment: This design is 1600 wide. Every check used to open a 1280x720 window, so the page's `max-width: 100%` shrank it and verify-frame reported `.magazine` as 1240 against Figma's 1600 — measuring the window, not the screen. Read by scripts/lib/screen-viewport.mjs; 1680 leaves room for the body's 20px gutters.

sourceClips.comment: Frames in the SOURCE FILE that are shorter than their own contents, read by scripts/check-frame-clip.mjs from prototypes/pathway-landing.figma.xml. An undeclared clip fails the check; declaring one records that the question was asked and answered rather than silently inherited. The house rule now requires Figma frames to show the full screen, so new extracts should have nothing here.

6953:22156.decision: Build the full content — 1507 tall, nothing clipped.
6953:22156.why: Asked rather than chosen. Both readings were internally consistent: the renderer gives 840 = 20 + 254 + 566 with the Outcomes pills cut through the middle and the whole Related learning block never drawn, and get_metadata gives content running to 1507. Taking either number on its own would have produced a confident, verified, wrong screen — 840 silently drops a third of the design and 1085 describes nothing at all. This frame predates the full-screen rule.

divergences.comment: Known, deliberate differences from Figma. Listed so they are decisions rather than drift.
divergences.headingUsesPrimitive: Figma colours the page title `color/grey/18` / `Shark` #2c2c31 — a PRIMITIVE. Primitives do not change between modes, so porting it verbatim would break dark mode, which CLAUDE.md forbids outright. The page uses --pf-text-primary. This is the one place the design file is not followed, and it is followed everywhere the rule is not at stake.
divergences.progressTrackHasNoVariable: The progress track is #d9d9d9, a raw hex bound to no variable at all — while the percentage text beside it does have one (`Progress bar - text percentage (light)`). A raw hex cannot be written on this project, so the track uses --pf-border-default, the nearest token that is actually a surface rule of that weight. Recorded as a real gap in the design file rather than a choice.
divergences.tabWidth: `.pf-tab` is captured at a fixed width: 40px, because that is the Figma component's default. Figma's own tabs here are 72, 59 and 116 wide. The width is overridden to content width in local CSS — page layout, not component appearance.
divergences.tabUnderline: dist/components.css carries no border-bottom and no descendant selectors anywhere: every rule is a single flat element rule, so .pf-tab[data-state="Selected"] changes only the colour. Figma draws a 2px themed rule under the selected tab, so the rule is local CSS and declared as GAP 1.
divergences.progressBarIsContainerOnly: `.pf-percentage-bar`, `.pf-square-progress-bar` and `.pf-table-progress-bar` are all outer flex boxes with no track and no fill — their Percentage/Progress axes were collapsed during capture, so the bar itself was never captured. Built in local CSS and asserted here.
divergences.selectionCardNotInLibrary: `Selection card` appears nowhere in dist/components.css, docs/components.html or tokens/_raw/ — and not in uncaptured-reasons.tsv either, so it is not a known exclusion. It is simply absent, exactly like `Clickable card` (F-018). Built in local CSS to Figma's measured values and asserted by the `frame` block.
divergences.horizontalScroll: `Horizontal scroll` is explicitly uncaptured — tokens/_raw/uncaptured-reasons.tsv: `no variant binds a colour variable in Figma — nothing to put in a stylesheet`. Built as local CSS.
divergences.shareIcon: Figma's Code Connect prop is `mhrIcon="addFullSize"` while the glyph actually drawn is a paper-plane share. The page follows the picture and uses assets/icons/share.svg. See observations.shareButtonPropDisagreesWithGlyph.

observations.comment: Things this file says that disagree with each other or with the design system. Reproduced or recorded exactly rather than reconciled, because picking whichever reading looks tidiest would be inventing a decision.
observations.frameClipsItsOwnContent: get_metadata and the renderer disagreed, and both were internally consistent. The renderer: frame 1600x840 = 20 + 254 + 566, and container 566 = 461 + 105 — so the Outcomes pills were cut off mid-height and the entire `Related learning` block at y=620 was below the cut and never drawn. get_metadata: frame 1085, container 1233, Outcomes 129, content running to 1507. The frame was fixed at a height shorter than its own content and Figma clipped the overflow — the same behaviour as the Case card at 74px with a 75px child, three orders of magnitude larger. Asked and answered: build the full content, so this screen is 1507 tall and nothing is clipped. RESOLVED AT SOURCE: a house rule now requires Figma frames to show the full screen rather than clip it, so future extracts should have the renderer and get_metadata agreeing and this question should not arise again. This screen predates the rule, which is why it is recorded rather than silently reconciled. Note what the rule cannot do on its own: it is a convention, not a check, and this pipeline exists because conventions are kept until they quietly are not. Where the two heights disagree, ASK — never pick the one that makes the build easier.
observations.twoSpacingScalesInOneFile: The file carries both naming schemes at once, resolving to the same numbers: `Spacing/sizing-small`=10 AND `Spacing/sizing-sm`=10; `Spacing/sizing-large`=20 AND `Spacing/sizing-md`=20; plus `Spacing/sizing-xs`=5 and `Spacing/sizing-xlarge`=40. The Selection card uses the new short names; everything else uses the old long ones. Both map onto --pf-space-*, so nothing is lost in the port — but the design system has two live names for one value.
observations.iconSizeUsedAsSpacing: `Icon-size-xxxs` is 0, and the Selection card uses it as a gap AND as vertical padding: `gap-[var(--icon-size-xxxs,0px)]`, `py-[var(--icon-size-xxxs,0px)]`, `p-[var(--icon-size-xxxs,0px)]`. An icon-size variable standing in for zero spacing. The port uses 0 and does not invent a spacing token for it.
observations.shareButtonPropDisagreesWithGlyph: The SHARE button's Code Connect snippet is `<mhr-icon mhrIcon="addFullSize" />` while the glyph Figma draws is a paper-plane share. The generated code and the rendered design disagree about which icon this is.
observations.emptyTagsOnEveryCard: Every Selection card ends with two `<mhr-tag [mhrTagText]="{ text: '' }" />` — two tags with no text. Reproduced as two empty tags rather than removed or filled: giving them words would be inventing content.
observations.outcomePillOverflows: The third Outcome pill's text is `whitespace-nowrap` inside `flex-[1_0_0]`, so it runs past its own box. Reproduced.
observations.fourIdenticalCards: All four `Selection card` instances carry the same title, the same E-Learning line, the same creator and the same view count. As with the three identical Case cards, this reads as unfinished work in Figma rather than a design decision — and giving each a different title would be inventing content.
observations.figmaWillNotRenderTheCards: The four Selection cards cannot be compared against a Figma render, because Figma will not draw them: they sit at y=620, below the frame's 840px clip, and get_screenshot returns a 1x1 image for them and for their whole `Related learning` container. The only evidence for that 40% of the screen is get_design_context and get_metadata, both saved verbatim in dsskill/runs/20260910-pathway-landing/context/. Said plainly because 'compared against the Figma render' is otherwise a claim this screen cannot support in full.
observations.magazineBackgroundSettledByRendering: The container beneath the white bar is Background/Theme (#fcf4f7), not Background/Secondary. Nothing in get_design_context said so — the fill is on a node whose own code was never fetched — and the first build had it neutral grey. Rendering the tabs node 6953:22200 alone, which shows the strip behind it, settled it in one call.

frame_comment: Machine-readable geometry, read by scripts/verify-frame.mjs. Every value is from the saved extract in dsskill/runs/. The heights are the METADATA heights — the content — because the renderer's heights are the clipped ones and the decision was to build the full content. See observations.frameClipsItsOwnContent.  The card internals, the masthead icons and the meta rows are asserted here too: they came from the extract and would otherwise be measured by nothing, which is the standing the subject field's width had the day it turned out to be 10px wrong (F-024). This matters more on this screen than on any other, because Figma will not render the four cards at all — see observations.figmaWillNotRenderTheCards — so an assertion against the saved extract is the ONLY thing that can check them.
